name: Validity conditions of the analytic vFFA model (categorical; p. 10)
value: m high compared with sin(thetaF); radius of curvature in the magnets large compared with the magnet length; fringe-field length much smaller than the magnet length
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Closed-orbit model assumption: hard-edge constant dipole field along the orbit inside the magnets, zero outside (categorical; p. 7)
value: dipole fields constant along the orbit within the magnets and zero elsewhere (hard-edge model); closed orbit fixed by Nc, betaF, betaD, r0, thetaF, gammaF
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Conclusion: proposed mitigation (RF in decoupled dispersion-suppressed straights) and planned longitudinal-dynamics simulations (categorical; p. 15)
value: proposed: RF in decoupled, dispersion-suppressed straights so arcs can use lower m-values; future study: longitudinal dynamics simulation for RF in suppressed straights and for RF distributed in dispersive arc drifts
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Conclusion caveat: high m-values needed to limit the excursion restrict the parameter space and make fields grow rapidly off orbit (categorical; p. 15)
value: high m-values required to minimise the excursion (needed for the RF design) limit the accessible parameter space and cause fields to grow rapidly away from the closed orbit
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Conclusion caveat: the analytic lattices must still be verified by numerical simulation and non-linear study (categorical; p. 15)
value: lattices from the analytic formalism must be verified by numerical simulation; non-linear properties to be studied for beam survival over many turns; further analytic iteration may lower dipole strengths
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Conclusion: direct vFFA alternatives to the RCS rings exist with stable (analytic) optics and realistic drift lengths and on-orbit fields (categorical; p. 15)
value: direct vFFA alternatives to the proposed RCS rings exist with stable optics; drift lengths and peak dipole strengths on orbit within realistic bounds
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Opportunities afforded by decoupled straights: multi-magnet injection/extraction kicks and dispersion suppression (categorical; p. 13)
value: injection/extraction systems kicking the beam over many magnets become feasible; horizontal-excursion FFA dispersion suppression schemes become applicable
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Condition for decoupled vFFA cells: both magnets at 90° inclination, which forces θF = θD, i.e. zero net bending (categorical; p. 12)
value: coupling terms of the Hamiltonian vanish for gamma = 90 deg; with gammaF = gammaD = 90 deg eq. (2.2) requires thetaF = thetaD; fully decoupled cells only with zero net bending (straights)
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Magnet inclination at which the transverse planes of a vFFA cell decouple (p. 12)
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Maximum allowable peak SC dipole field on orbit adopted as design limit (LHC main dipole operating field; MuCol M17 p. 10)
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Principal design objectives of the vFFA proposal (categorical statement; MuCol M17 p. 10)
value: match the RCS footprint (5990 m circumference for stage 1); peak SC dipole field on orbit below 8.3 T (LHC main dipole); minimise the vertical excursion between injection and extraction (RF cavity and magnet apertures); drift lengths of at least 1 m
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: vFFA dispersion formula D_z = 1/m (formula, categorical; eq. 3.6)
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Rationale for dispersion-suppressed RF straights: fewer RF constraints, lower arc m-values, lower pole-tip fields (categorical; §3.3)
value: RF confined to dispersion-suppressed regions relaxes arc design, allows lower m-values, hence lower pole-tip fields for the same on-orbit field (or higher on-orbit fields), may reduce distributed RF needs and frees the decoupled-tune working point
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Caveat: the dispersion suppressor principle relies on linear approximations of the dispersive behaviour (categorical; p. 15)
value: valid only while linear approximations of the dispersive behaviour hold; a higher-order implementation exists for horizontal-excursion FFAs (ref. [10])
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Required phase advance of the dispersion suppressor in the dispersive (vertical) plane (p. 14)
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: FFA dispersion suppressor rule: D2 = (D1 + D3)/2 with 180° vertical phase advance in a decoupled straight (formula, categorical; eq. 3.7)
value: three cell types with dispersions D1 (initial), D2 (suppressor), D3 (final); D2 = (D1 + D3)/2 fixes the suppressor m-value; phase advance of the suppressor in the dispersive (vertical z) plane = 180 deg; the suppressor must be a decoupled straight with 90 deg inclination; D3 = 0 gives complete suppression
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: FODO cell model assumption: F and D magnets independent in size and dipole strength, but equal m (categorical; p. 7)
value: dimensions and dipole strengths of the F and D magnets independent; normalised field gradient m equal in both magnets
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Advantages claimed for fixed fields in muon acceleration (categorical; p. 5)
value: ramp rate no longer limits the acceleration rate (only the available integrated RF gradient does); no eddy-current losses; fixed strengths suit superconducting magnets; no ramped-magnet power converters
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: vFFA magnet focusing terms of the body Hamiltonian, eq. (2.9) (categorical; p. 9)
value: skew-quadrupole-like focusing term proportional to cos(gamma); normal-quadrupole focusing term proportional to sin(gamma); weak focusing terms proportional to 1/rho^2
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Normalised transverse emittance assumed (both planes) for the good-field-region peak field evaluation of Table 2.3 (MuCol M17)
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Method used for the Table 2.3 good-field-region peak field (categorical statement; MuCol M17)
value: 25 um normalised emittance in both planes; beam size projected onto the cartesian xy planes with the Mais-Ripken decoupling parametrisation; scaling law applied to evaluate the field away from the closed orbit
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Inclination of each magnet set by the horizontal displacement from its midplane, γ ≃ m x (formula, categorical; eq. 2.8)
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Fallback options if direct matching fails: insertion phase advances multiple of 180°, or adiabatic inclination transition (categorical; p. 14)
value: design the straight insertion with phase advances in both planes equal to a multiple of 180 deg (optically transparent), or adiabatically vary the inclination over several arc cells towards 90 deg at the cost of a larger ring
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: vFFA optics: all curved vFFA lattices have intrinsic transverse coupling (categorical; p. 7)
value: 2nd-order field components act as a skew quadrupole at the peak-vertical-field region (zero normal quadrupole there) while the normal quadrupole is non-zero elsewhere, so all curved vFFA lattices have intrinsic horizontal-vertical coupling
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: vFFA limitation: vertically moving beam centroid requires large-aperture cavities (categorical; p. 7)
value: higher-energy orbits are stacked above lower-energy orbits, so the beam centroid moves vertically between injection and extraction and large-aperture cavities are required
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: vFFA limitation: specialised magnet design needed for scaling-law fields (categorical; p. 7)
value: a specialised magnet design is required to achieve the high dipole fields and the exponential field profile along the vertical gap
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Matching rule: the m-value must be the same in arc and straight cells so that closed orbits match at all energies (categorical; p. 14)
value: m-value consistent between arc cells and straight cells (closed-orbit matching at all energies); linear-optics matching between the coupled u,v planes of the arc and the x,z planes of the straight is non-trivial
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: vFFA closed-orbit property: geometrically identical orbit for all energies, translated vertically; constant tune (categorical)
value: closed orbit geometrically identical for all energies, translated vertically with energy; tune constant over the acceleration cycle
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Peak on-orbit magnetic field of the vFFA booster arcs (synthetic screening range)
vFFA quasi-isochronism: slip factor η = αc − 1/γ² tends to zero at high γ (categorical; eq. 1.2)
value: eta = alpha_c - 1/gamma^2 = (dtau/tau)/(dP/P) tends to zero for highly relativistic particles since alpha_c = 0; the vFFA is quasi-isochronous for sufficiently high momentum
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Motivation for a vFFA alternative to RCS4 (categorical statement; MuCol M17 p. 10)
value: RCS4 has the highest path length difference over its acceleration cycle, which may increase RF tuning requirements
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Scope of the MuCol M17 report: analytic vFFA alternative to one or more RCS rings, with peak-field mitigation proposals (categorical; abstract and p. 7)
value: FFA (vFFA) as alternative to one or more RCS rings of the MuCol chain; analytic FODO lattices with footprints, energy ranges and on-orbit peak fields comparable to RCS1 and RCS4; mitigation of peak field via decoupled, dispersion-suppressed straights
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: vFFA limitation: reverse-bend magnets required for two-plane stability, reducing spatial efficiency (categorical; p. 7)
value: sign of the quadrupole component is fixed by the sign of the dipole field, so stability in two planes requires reverse-bend magnets; spatial efficiency below the rigidity/peak-field maximum
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: vFFA scaling law: dipole field grows exponentially with the vertical coordinate (formula, categorical; eq. 1.1)
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Closed-orbit equations of a straight (zero-net-bend) vFFA FODO cell, eqs (3.1)-(3.5) (formula, categorical; p. 13)
value: thetaD = thetaF; gammaD = gammaF; rhoF = LF/sin(thetaF); rhoD = LD/sin(thetaD); Ls = (Lc - LF - LD)/cos(thetaF)
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Straight vFFA cell at 90° inclination is equivalent to the tested straight horizontal-excursion FFA cell (categorical; p. 13)
value: a straight vFFA cell with 90 deg orbit inclination is entirely equivalent to the straight horizontal-excursion FFA cell proposed and tested in the report's ref. [8]
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)

name: Method by which the Table 2.3 tunes were obtained: decoupled tunes from the eigenvalues of the 4D cell transfer matrix (categorical; p. 10)
value: periodic 4D cell transfer matrix from magnet matrices (eq. 2.9 Hamiltonian) and drifts; decoupled tunes = arguments of its eigenvalues
source_title: Tentative design of the FFA (MuCol Milestone Report No. 17)
